Zombie Panic! Source - How can I use commands? (rcon_password / rcon <command>)
Console Command List - Valve Developer Community
Source engine banid usage: banid <minutes> <userid | uniqueid> { kick }

notes: Source-engine dedicated server (srcds, mod dir 'zps', LinuxGSM start line '-game zps ... -port 27015'). RCON is stock Valve Source RCON on the game port (27015 TCP by default; the port comes from the -port launch argument, there is no separate RCON port) and is switched on simply by setting rcon_password in zps/cfg/server.cfg. Confidence is low because no ZPS-specific document lists the commands recorded here: they are the stock srcds engine commands (status/kickid/banid/removeid/say) documented by Valve's own wiki and corroborated by Source-engine command references, and the exact status line layout is inferred from Source SDK 2013 rather than observed on ZPS. playerId is the per-session userid printed by status, NOT a Steam ID: both kickid and banid accept it, and banid resolves it to the account id when it writes the ban, which is why it is the safer target for a tool that lists players and acts immediately. banid does not disconnect the player by itself, hence the trailing 'kick' argument; a ban only survives a restart after 'writeid', and the engine appends it to cfg/banned_user.cfg as 'banid <minutes> <id>'. No live unban is recorded under commands because removeid takes the Steam ID, not the userid - it is recorded as banList.liveUnban instead, and must also be followed by 'writeid'. ZPS 3.x additionally ships its own admin system (zps/data/adminsystem/adminsystem.json, flags a-z incl. 'i' for rcon) with its own commands: 'status_full' (prints !entindex, #id, name, steamid64, team), 'admin kick #22 "Trolling on the server"', 'admin ban #22 "60" "Trolling again"' (duration in minutes) and 'admin unban U:1:38199539' (SteamID3 without brackets). Those are documented for ZPS specifically but target three different identifier forms and depend on an admin entry, so they were not used as the primary set; they are the fallback if the engine commands are found to be blocked. status on ZPS prints SteamID3 ([U:1:38199539]) per that admin guide; the parse pattern also accepts the older STEAM_x:y:z form. There is no motd command - the MOTD is the motd.txt file (motdfile cvar).
